end.summary:
Practised multiplying by 10, 100 and 1000 using place value.
Used place-value zeros for 250, 2500, 12500 and 360.
Solved 25 × 36 by splitting it into 25 × 30 and 25 × 6, then adding to get 900.
Double-and-half method was discussed; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Sameer practised using place value to multiply by 10, 100 and 1000, and split 25 × 36 into two smaller products. They explained why 25 × 30 is 750 and combined it with 150 to get 900. There was a mix-up with the double-and-half method, but they later changed 24 to 12 and reached 50 × 12 = 600 (correctAfterLastSeen). At home, practise a few examples by saying aloud which digit changes when multiplying by 10, 100 or 1000.
